title: Objects
explain: Objects in JavaScript are collections of key-value pairs that store related data and functions together. You create objects using curly braces {} and access their properties using dot notation (object.property) or bracket notation (object['property']). Objects help organize code by grouping related information, like storing a person's name, age, and email in one place.
exercise: Create an object called 'book' with properties: title, author, and pages. Then log the book's title to the console.
tip: Remember that object property names are case-sensitive—person.Name is different from person.name. Use consistent naming conventions to avoid bugs.
